page: Microsoft Azure F48als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Falsv6 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable and runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read operations reaching top-tier status and uncached large-block read/write operations placing in the top 25%. Single-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. The hardware excels at compute-heavy tasks, demonstrating top-tier performance in software compilation with Clang, image processing, and medium-model (7B) LLM text generation.

The F48als_v6 offers a highly cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that require dense CPU resources without a corresponding demand for large memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is its low memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core and the lack of local storage, which makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data caching. However, its high clock speed and dedicated core allocation make it an excellent fit for workloads such as software compilation, image processing, web serving, and compute-intensive batch processing.
